title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Perioperative Sodium-Glucose Transporter 2 Inhibition in Cardiac Surgery Patients: An Open-Label Randomized Pilot Study.
authors: Snel LIP; Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Lankadeva YR; Plummer MP; Preckel B; Zuurbier CJ; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; Hulst AH
publication_type: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; JOUR; Journal article
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods 2.2 Study Participants: adult elective CPB-assisted cardiac surgery patients. Methods 2.4 Intervention: empagliflozin 10 mg daily from 3 days before to 2 days after surgery vs standard care. Randomized open-label design (2.1–2.3). Outcomes reported include diuresis, fluid balance, vasoactive support, blood pressure/heart rate, postoperative AF, and CK-MB (2.5, Results 3.1–3.5).
agent_rationale: Adults undergoing elective cardiopulmonary bypass-assisted cardiac surgery were randomized to perioperative empagliflozin (10 mg daily from 3 days preop to 2 days postop) versus standard care, with hemodynamic and safety outcomes reported. This matches the population, exposure, comparator, and outcomes for inclusion.

title: Dapagliflozin for inpatient hyperglycemia in cardiac surgery patients with type 2 diabetes: randomised controlled trial (Dapa-Hospital trial).
authors: Kuchay MS; Khatana P; Mishra M; Surendran P; Kaur P; Wasir JS; Gill HK; Singh A; Jain R; Kohli C; Bakshi G; Radhika V; Saheer S; Singh MK; Mishra SK
publication_type: Randomized Controlled Trial; Journal Article; JOUR; Journal article
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods—Eligibility criteria: “All consecutive patients admitted for cardiac surgery… Patients with T2D… were deemed eligible” (Material and methods, Eligibility criteria). Procedures/Randomization: “On the day of transition (day 2 of surgery)… all patients were randomized to receive either dapagliflozin 10 mg daily plus a basal‑bolus regimen or a basal‑bolus insulin regimen” (Procedures). Study outcomes: primary mean daily blood glucose; safety outcomes included severe ketonemia/DKA and hypoglycemia; hospital complications including acute kidney injury, pleural effusion requiring intervention, wound infection, arrhythmia, mortality; and length of stay (Study outcomes, Safety outcomes, Table 3).
agent_rationale: Adult patients with T2D admitted for open cardiac surgery (CABG and/or valvular) were randomized in the early postoperative period to dapagliflozin 10 mg daily plus basal–bolus insulin versus basal–bolus insulin alone. Reports efficacy (glycemia) and safety outcomes (hypoglycemia, severe ketonemia/DKA, AKI, complications, LOS). RCT design with comparator.

title: Empagliflozin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Undergoing On-Pump CABG: The POST-CABGDM Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Pitta FG; Lima EG; Tavares CAM; Martins EB; Rached FH; Moreira EM; Mioto BM; Lottenberg SA; Bolta PMP; Justino LG; Favarato D; Carvalho LNS; Pinesi HT; Barbosa CTM; Dallan LAO; Dallan LRP; Barbosa MHM; Kalil Filho R; de Lemos JA; Serrano CV
publication_type: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Pragmatic Clinical Trial; JOUR; Journal article
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods—Trial Design and Population: patients aged ≥18 with T2DM undergoing planned on-pump CABG randomized 1:1 (n=145 operated; empagliflozin n=71, control n=74). Interventions and Procedures: empagliflozin 25 mg/day for ≥3 months pre-op, discontinued 72 h before surgery; control received standard care. Study Outcomes: primary—postoperative AKI within 7 days (KDIGO/AKIN/RIFLE); secondary—30-day AF and type 5 MI; safety—ketoacidosis, UTI, pneumonia, wound infection. Results: AKI 22.5% vs 39.1% (RR 0.57, P=0.03).
agent_rationale: Adults with T2DM scheduled for elective on-pump CABG were randomized to preoperative empagliflozin 25 mg daily (stopped 72 h pre-op) vs standard care. Primary outcome was AKI within 7 days; secondary/safety outcomes assessed to 30 days. Open cardiac surgery population with appropriate comparator and perioperative SGLT2i exposure; reports prespecified efficacy and safety outcomes.

title: Evaluation of the effect of empagliflozin on prevention of atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
authors: Zarei B; Fazli B; Tayyebi M; Abbasi Teshnizi M; Moeinipour A; Javedanfar O; Javidi Dasht Bayaz R; Rahmati M; Ghavami V; Amini S; Mohammadpour AH
publication_type: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; JOUR; Journal article
agent_eligibility_evidence: Materials and methods: adults (18–70 years) undergoing elective off‑pump CABG were enrolled and randomized (n=82). Randomization and blinding: empagliflozin 10 mg vs matching placebo started 3 days pre‑op and continued for the first three postoperative days (6 total doses). Outcomes: postoperative arrhythmias during the first 72 h (including POAF, VT/VF, PVCs) and CRP on POD3 reported, plus ECG/laboratory/hemodynamic outcomes.
agent_rationale: Randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial of perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor in adult cardiac surgery patients with relevant outcomes.

title: The effects of sodium-glucose transporter 2 inhibition on cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: An open-label randomized pilot study.
authors: Snel LIP; Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Rampanelli E; Lankadeva YR; Plummer MP; Preckel B; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; Hulst AH
publication_type: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Clinical Trial, Phase IV; JOUR; Journal article
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods—Study participants: adults 18–90 years scheduled for CPB-assisted cardiac surgery. Methods—Intervention: empagliflozin 10 mg daily from 3 days before surgery to POD2 vs no intervention/standard care. Methods—Outcomes: AKI incidence within 7 days per KDIGO; metabolic safety incl. ketones, ketoacidosis, glycemic control; biomarkers. Results: ITT n=55; AKI 20% vs 66.7% (empagliflozin vs control); no ketoacidosis observed.
agent_rationale: Open-label randomized controlled pilot trial in adult patients undergoing elective cardiopulmonary bypass cardiac surgery; perioperative empagliflozin 10 mg started 3 days pre-op through post-op day 2 versus standard care; reports AKI incidence (KDIGO) within 7 days and safety outcomes (ketoacidosis, hypoglycemia). Meets all inclusion criteria.

title: Initiation of peri-operative SGLT2 inhibitor reduces mortality and cardiovascular events after surgical aortic valve replacement
authors: Yan, J.; McKinnerney, J.; Al Janabi, T.; Korgaonkar, N.; Kashyap, R.
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods – Patient selection and exposure groups: adults ≥18 who underwent SAVR; exposure defined as first-time SGLT2 inhibitor use within 30 days pre-op, compared to matched non-users. Outcomes section: primary outcomes 1-year all-cause mortality and MACE; secondary outcomes include MI, cerebral infarction, AF/flutter, hospital readmission, UTI, and AKI. Results/Table 2 report these postoperative outcomes.
agent_rationale: Meets all criteria: adult humans undergoing open cardiac surgery (SAVR); exposure is initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor within 30 days preoperatively; comparator is matched non-users; retrospective cohort with outcomes reported (mortality, MACE, MI, stroke, AF/flutter, readmission, AKI, UTI).

title: Evaluation of the effect of empagliflozin on prevention of atrial fibrillation after heart valve surgery: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
authors: YazdFazeli M; Samimi S; Abbasi Teshnizi M; Hoseinikhah H; Moeinipour A; Javedanfar O; Ghavami V; Abedi F; Amini S; Fazli B; Mohammadpour AH
journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
agent_eligibility_evidence: Abstract states: “110 patients undergoing elective heart valve surgery were randomized to oral empagliflozin 10 mg daily or placebo from 3 days pre-op to 3 days post-op… The primary outcome was POAF incidence within 72 h… No significant differences were observed in adverse event rates.”
agent_rationale: Meets all inclusion criteria: adult patients undergoing open cardiac valve surgery; randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial; perioperative empagliflozin exposure (3 days pre-op to 3 days post-op); comparator placebo; reports efficacy/safety outcomes (POAF and adverse events).

title: Dapagliflozin and Acute Kidney Injury Following Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Hulst AH; de Oliveira NPM; Niesten ED; Wietsma NE; Gerritse BM; Scohy TV; Rettig TCD; Snellen FTF; Voogd MF; Godfried MB; de Boer RN; Wink J; van der Werff LMM; Cobbaert CM; Ruhaak LR; Eberl S; Preckel B; Hollmann MW; Schenk J; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; MERCURI-2 Study Group
agent_eligibility_evidence: Abstract: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial in adults undergoing elective cardiac surgery; intervention dapagliflozin 10 mg started the day before surgery through postoperative day 2; comparator placebo; primary outcome AKI within 7 days post-op; adverse events reported.
agent_rationale: RCT in adults undergoing elective cardiac surgery testing perioperative dapagliflozin vs placebo with postoperative outcomes reported.

title: Differential Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and SGLT2 Inhibitor Add-on Therapy on Outcomes Following Cardiac Surgery: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
authors: Biswas S; Wahba A; Srivastava Y; Kumar K; Chintagumpala V; Said SM
agent_eligibility_evidence: Retrospective TriNetX cohort of adults undergoing CABG or open valve surgery; analyses compare combination GLP-1 RA + SGLT2 inhibitor vs GLP-1 RA monotherapy and vs SGLT2i monotherapy with outcomes including 365-day mortality. Abstract states effects of add-on therapy on outcomes following cardiac surgery and does not clarify preoperative/perioperative exposure window, raising concern that exposure may be postoperative.
agent_rationale: Adults undergoing open cardiac surgery with comparisons involving SGLT2 inhibitor exposure are described, but the abstract does not specify whether SGLT2i use was preoperative/perioperative versus initiated postoperatively. Timing of exposure relative to surgery is crucial for eligibility and remains unclear from metadata alone.

title: SGLT2 Inhibition as a Perioperative Cardiorenal Stabilizer in Cardiac Surgery: Integrated Clinical Cohort and Pleiotropic Network-Based Pharmacological Analysis.
authors: Onar LC; Guner E; Yilmaz I
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods—Study Design and Patient Population: adult T2DM patients undergoing open heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CABG, valve, combined). Methods—Treatment Exposure and Patient Stratification: chronic SGLT2 inhibitor use ≥90 days pre-op; routinely stopped ~48 h pre-op and reinitiated after discharge; non-users managed with other agents (comparator). Outcomes—Clinical Outcomes, Definitions, and Follow-Up: primary outcome 12‑month unplanned rehospitalization; Results and Table 3 report effect estimates comparing SGLT2 users vs non-users.
agent_rationale: Meets all inclusion criteria: adult humans undergoing open cardiac surgery; exposure is preoperative/perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor therapy with comparator group; retrospective cohort design reporting postoperative outcomes.

title: Preoperative Exposure to Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors and Acute Kidney Injury After Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Single-Centre Cohort Study With Overlap Weighting Propensity Score Analysis.
authors: Ruste M; Vieira A; Le Guennec-Lux Y; Berthod C; Pozzi M; Mewton N; Fellahi JL; Jacquet-Lagrèze M
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods—Participants: Adults undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass; exposure defined as preoperative long-term SGLT2i vs no SGLT2i (Data Handling). Comparator present (unexposed). Outcomes reported include AKI within 7 days post-op (primary endpoint) and safety (euglycemic ketoacidosis, UTI) (Results; Table 2; Figure 3). Study design: single-centre retrospective cohort with propensity score weighting (Study Design/Statistical Analysis).
agent_rationale: Adult cardiac surgery cohort with CPB comparing preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure versus no exposure; outcomes include postoperative AKI and safety events; retrospective comparative design fits inclusion.

title: Perioperative dapagliflozin in diabetic patients undergoing cardiac surgery: the DAPA-CS trial.
authors: Li Z; Chen R; Han J; Zhou H; Zeng Z; Zhao Y; Liu S; Zhang H; Zheng Z
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods—Participants and intervention: adults with type 2 diabetes scheduled for elective on-pump cardiac surgery; randomized 1:1 to dapagliflozin 10 mg/day perioperatively (≥3 days pre-op, held on surgery day, resumed post-op to POD5) versus standard care without SGLT2i. Outcomes: primary hs-cTnI at 48 h; key secondary AKI by KDIGO; safety outcomes include DKA. Results/Figure 1B–F: 164 patients underwent surgery (majority isolated on-pump CABG; some AVR), comparator present, and efficacy/safety outcomes reported.
agent_rationale: Randomized controlled trial of perioperative dapagliflozin versus standard care in adult patients undergoing on-pump cardiac surgery, reporting prespecified efficacy (hs-cTnI, AKI) and safety (DKA) outcomes.

title: Enhanced recovery mitigates sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors associated mobility decline in valve surgery patients.
authors: Xu C; Chen M; Lu E; Zhang X; You H; Zhao X; Sun Y; Xu X
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods 2.1 Study design and population: adults (18–75) with VHD undergoing elective valve surgery within ERAS; QT group received SGLT2i (dapagliflozin/empagliflozin) as part of quadruple therapy, continued until the day before surgery and restarted post-op; TT group without SGLT2i. Outcomes assessed at multiple perioperative timepoints; Table 1 reports ERAS metrics (ICU duration, mobilization times).
agent_rationale: Adult valve surgery patients in a retrospective cohort comparing perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor use (dapagliflozin/empagliflozin) versus no SGLT2i; drugs continued to day before surgery and resumed post-anesthesia. Comparator present; outcomes include ICU duration, mobilization times, ADL and other perioperative measures.

title: Effects of dapagliflozin on main pulmonary artery diameter in patients undergoing mitral valve replacement: a retrospective observational study.
authors: Wang D; Liu P; Chen X; Hu H; Wang H; Zhang Z; Liu X
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods 2.1–2.2: adult patients ≥18 undergoing MVR (open surgery) between 2020–2025; Dapagliflozin group received 10 mg daily preoperatively for at least 2 weeks; controls had no SGLT2i. Exclusions ensured surgical cohort (no transcatheter; excluded concomitant CABG/emergent/redo). Outcomes (2.5) and Results/Table 2 report perioperative changes in MPA diameter and other echo/biomarker parameters.
agent_rationale: Meets all criteria: adult humans undergoing open cardiac surgery (mitral valve replacement). Exposure: preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for ≥2 weeks) vs no SGLT2i control. Study design: retrospective observational with comparator. Outcomes reported within the perioperative window include echocardiographic and biomarker measures (MPA diameter, PASP, LVEF, TAPSE, RVBD, NT-proBNP).

title: Impact of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors on Acute Kidney Injury Post Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Retrospective Cohort Study and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Zhou X; Pan Y; Hua K; Yang X
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods 2.1 Study Population: consecutive OPCABG patients (age 18–80) 2018–2023; SGLT2i protocol: dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for ≥3 months preop, stopped 72 h before surgery; comparator: non-SGLT2i users with 1:3 PSM. Primary outcome: postoperative AKI within 48 h; secondary outcomes include in-hospital death and CRRT (Table 2).
agent_rationale: Adults undergoing open cardiac surgery (OPCABG) with preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure were compared with non-users; outcomes included postoperative AKI and safety endpoints. Study design is original retrospective cohort with comparator.

title: Preoperative SGLT2i therapy and acute kidney injury in patients undergoing emergency and urgent coronary artery bypass grafting - A causal inference framework.
authors: Kolland M; Sartori S; Klivinyi C; Schörghuber M; Pannold J; Knez I; Kirsch AH; Schreiber N
publication_type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods 2.2: Included adults undergoing urgent (<48 h) or emergent (≤12 h) isolated CABG with indications for SGLT2i; exposure defined as SGLT2i use within two weeks before surgery; comparator = no SGLT2i. Methods 2.3: Primary outcome CSA-AKI (KDIGO); secondary outcomes KRT, ICU length of stay, 30-day mortality; safety outcome postoperative DKA. Results 3.2–3.3: Comparative results reported between SGLT2i users (n=135) and non-users (n=349).
agent_rationale: Adults undergoing open cardiac surgery (urgent/emergent isolated CABG) with preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure within 2 weeks versus non-users; retrospective comparative study reporting perioperative AKI and safety outcomes.

title: Postoperative Ketoacidosis in Cardiac Surgery: Incidence, Analytical Profile, and Association With Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors-A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Ginestal-Calvo J; Flordelís-Lasierra JL; Pérez-Vela JL; Campos-Bermejo L; Coso-Garrido C; Blanco-Carrasco L; Galiano-Carrilero C; Domínguez-Aguado H; Renes-Carreño E
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
publication_type: Journal Article; Observational Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods—Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria: adults ≥18 undergoing elective valvular/coronary/aortic or combined procedures. Perioperative Management of SGLT2 Inhibitors: continued until hospital admission, then withheld; last dose 12–24 h pre-op. Results: 107 patients included; SGLT2i users vs nonusers compared for postoperative ketoacidosis and clinical outcomes (see Tables 2–4).
agent_rationale: Prospective observational cohort of adult patients undergoing elective open cardiac surgery with a comparator group (SGLT2 inhibitor users vs nonusers). Exposure occurred preoperatively/perioperatively (last dose typically 12–24 hours before surgery). Reports safety outcomes including postoperative ketoacidosis incidence and clinical outcomes (ICU stay, mechanical ventilation, reintervention, mortality). Meets all inclusion criteria.

title: Impact of SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy on Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
authors: Taghiyev ZT; Beier LM; Leweling C; Gunkel S; Sadowski KM; Assmus B; Boening A
publication_type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
agent_eligibility_evidence: Abstract: “53 cardiac surgical patients on SGLT2i therapy… were compared with 447 other HF patients… After 1:1… 33 vs 33. The primary endpoint was change in eGFR 36 hours after surgery… SGLT2i may have nephroprotective effects in patients undergoing heart surgery with extracorporeal circulation.”
agent_rationale: Observational comparative study of cardiac surgical patients on preoperative SGLT2 inhibitors versus controls, assessing postoperative renal outcomes. Population appears adult open cardiac surgery with extracorporeal circulation; exposure is preoperative SGLT2i; comparator present; reports postoperative eGFR and other renal outcomes.

title: Retrospective Chart Review of Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis Rates and Outcomes Postimplementation of Sodium Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use Stoppage 5 Days Before Open Heart Surgery.
authors: Auerbach JS; Alnajar A; Patel SS; Gershengorn HB; Lamelas J; Perez D; Aljure OD; Ferreira TD; Gonzalez LA; Cabrera JL
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
publication_type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods/Participants: Adult open heart surgery patients; patients <18 years excluded; surgeries included CABG and valve/aortic procedures (Table 2). Exposure: Patients on SGLT2i instructed to stop 5 days preoperatively vs non–SGLT2i users (Abstract; Methods—Exposures). Comparator: present (non-users). Outcomes: eDKA within 24 hours postsurgery plus CVICU and hospital LOS, mortality, and infections, with results reported (Tables 3–4, 6). Sample: 540 total; 48 SGLT2i users.
agent_rationale: Meets all inclusion criteria: adult humans undergoing open cardiac surgery with preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure compared against non-users and reports perioperative outcomes.

title: Preoperative dapagliflozin use and cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: A single-center retrospective cohort study.
authors: Chen Z; Liu K; Liu X; Wu B; Huang Z; Xing C; Mao H
agent_eligibility_evidence: Retrospective cohort of consecutive patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass; exposure: preoperative dapagliflozin use; comparator: no dapagliflozin; outcomes: CSA-AKI within 7 days, dialysis, death, recovery, length of stay.
agent_rationale: Metadata clearly indicates an adult cardiac surgery cohort with cardiopulmonary bypass, exposure to preoperative dapagliflozin (an SGLT2 inhibitor), a comparator group without dapagliflozin, and relevant postoperative outcomes. Study design (retrospective cohort) with appropriate comparator fits inclusion criteria.

title: Effects of Sodium-Glucose Transporter 2 Inhibitors (SGLT2-I) in Patients With Ischemic Heart Disease (IHD) Treated by Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting via MiECC: Inflammatory Burden, and Clinical Outcomes at 5 Years of Follow-Up.
authors: Sardu C; Massetti M; Testa N; Martino LD; Castellano G; Turriziani F; Sasso FC; Torella M; De Feo M; Santulli G; Paolisso G; Marfella R
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods: Adults >18 with multivessel CHD undergoing CABG via MiECC; T2DM patients classified as “SGLT2-I users” if they had used SGLT2i ≥6 months pre-CABG; empagliflozin 10 or 25 mg once daily (Materials and Methods). Comparator groups: T2DM non–SGLT2i users and non-T2DM (Table 1). Outcomes: all-cause death, cardiac death, non-fatal MI, stroke, repeat revascularization, composite endpoint at 1 and 5 years (Study Endpoints; Table 2).
agent_rationale: Observational multicenter cohort of adults undergoing open cardiac surgery (CABG via MiECC). Exposure group was preoperative/ongoing SGLT2 inhibitor therapy (empagliflozin 10–25 mg daily for ≥6 months before CABG) compared with T2DM patients not on SGLT2i and a non-diabetic cohort. Reports clinical efficacy/safety outcomes (all-cause death, cardiac death, MI, stroke, repeat revascularization, composite) at 1 and 5 years.
